summary.text: A 21-year-old male presented with intermittent chest pain for 4 months worsening with shortness of breath for 2 weeks after ascending to a 4,800-m plateau, with chest pain 3–4 times per week, chest tightness and shortness of breath triggered by mild activity, two episodes of amaurosis fugax and recent weight loss of about 2.5 kg. Earlier headaches were relieved by ibuprofen, and pre-altitude ECG and echocardiography were normal.

He had room-air oxygen saturation of 80% with cyanotic lips and P2 greater than A2. ECG showed right axis deviation with possible right ventricular enlargement. Echocardiography showed right atrial and ventricular enlargement, moderate tricuspid regurgitation, estimated sPAP of about 55 mmHg and mPAP 36 mmHg, and chest CT showed right-predominant cardiomegaly. The final diagnosis was HAPH.

He returned to an area below 1,500 m within 48 h and received no pharmacological or other specific interventions. Follow-up echocardiography 6 days later showed sPAP of about 47 mmHg and mPAP of 31 mmHg, and one month later pulmonary artery pressures had completely normalized.

summary.text: A 20-year-old male presented with intermittent exertional dyspnea for 5 months worsening with amaurosis fugax for 1 week, after ascending to a 4,300-m plateau 18 months earlier. One week before presentation, after routine training, he had amaurosis fugax with a brief loss of consciousness relieved by low-flow oxygen. Past history included unspecified hypoglycemia, and pre-altitude ECG and echocardiography were normal.

Room-air oxygen saturation was 82%, with a normal neurological examination and a 6-minute walk distance of 550 m. ECG showed right axis deviation with T-wave inversion suggesting right ventricular strain. Echocardiography showed right atrial and ventricular enlargement, moderate tricuspid regurgitation, estimated sPAP of about 56 mmHg and mPAP of about 36 mmHg, and chest CT showed right-predominant cardiomegaly. The final diagnosis was HAPH.

Because of occupational constraints he could not return promptly to low altitude and was managed with daily low-flow oxygen for over 16 h, strict limitation of physical activity and primarily bed rest. After 24 days, follow-up echocardiography showed mild progression of right heart enlargement, sPAP of about 47 mmHg and mPAP of 31 mmHg.
